commits.message: Research: record Native Host v1 Rust boundary
Research: record Native Host reuse lineage
Research: make native output loss fail closed

pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fresh Stage Research re-entry for roadmap stage **Native Host v1 — Rust** after the CAP Core v1 boundary work.

This PR is **research/architecture only**. It adds no Rust toolchain, binary, public tool, local-execution grant, process launcher, PTY implementation or sandbox.

### Sequencing lock

```text
#159 -> #165 -> #166 -> #167 -> #168 -> #169 -> Native Host v1
```

This branch is stacked on #169 only to research the intended post-Core boundary. **Do not merge it into the current #169 base while #169 still needs exact-head acceptance**, because that would move #169's head. Refresh against the accepted/frozen Core before production implementation.

## Stage Research decision

```text
NATIVE_HOST_V1_RESEARCH_DECISION_V1
stage_decision=NARROW
implementation_language=RUST
implementation_authority=POST_CORE_FREEZE_ONLY
first_slice=WINDOWS_PROCESS_LIFECYCLE
ipc=SHORT_LIVED_LENGTH_FRAMED_STDIO
host_durable_state=NONE
pty=FOLLOWUP_SLICE_AFTER_PROCESS_SUBSTRATE
sandbox=SEPARATE_SECURITY_REENTRY
public_tool_change=NO
```

The merged #132 decision was correctly `DEFER / future_native_language=UNRESOLVED` on 2026-08-28. The stage question has changed: #168/#169 establish the Core adapter boundary and ROADMAP now explicitly selects Rust for the narrow post-Core native host. This re-entry does **not** reopen a broad "rewrite CAP in Rust" question.

## Stage goal

```text
ordinary ChatGPT
 -> CAP semantic capability
 -> CAP Core
      authorization / grants
      WorkingState / attempts / reconciliation
      Verification Kernel / Finish Gate
 -> capability-specific adapter
 -> Rust Native Host v1
      process tree / native handles / Job Objects
      bounded launch / cancellation / cleanup receipts
 -> operating system
```

The host executes an **already-authorized bounded operation** and returns evidence. It never plans, grants/renews authority, owns WorkingState, decides project PASS or task DONE.

## Current project baseline and lineage

| Role | Prior owner/source | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| General planning | ordinary ChatGPT | KEEP |
| Capability authorization | project CAP Core | KEEP |
| WorkingState / reconciliation | project Core | KEEP |
| Verification / Finish Gate | project Kernel / Finish Gate | KEEP |
| Agent-host source reference | Codex reference-only | KEEP |
| Native systems execution | no canonical baseline role | NEW / SELECTED_NARROW |
| historical Rust-first CAP runtime | `chat/rust-relay-server` | REJECT as architecture; ADAPT selected low-level mechanics only |

Historical project source inspected at `BogdanAIP/chat-agent-platform@347e798fcef1c7a6ed7242553ea9de2f444366db`:

- `reaper.rs` has useful bounded spawn/kill/reap patterns but only process-local `Child::kill`, not the new Job/tree boundary;
- `job.rs` owns durable job/idempotency state that would now duplicate Core WorkingState/attempt ownership;
- `transport/protocol.rs` is HTTP relay/cache and is the wrong boundary for private local native IPC.

Therefore the old Rust-first tree is reference material, not a branch to revive.

## Architecture primitives and adjacent domains

| Primitive | Direct engineering domain | Guarantee sought | Boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| per-operation host lifetime | OS process lifecycle / supervision | one native owner and one crash domain per attempt | no persistent service/session semantics |
| length-framed anonymous-pipe IPC | local IPC / protocol framing | bounded unambiguous message boundaries without a discoverable endpoint | transport receipt is not effect success |
| one-active-attempt host state machine | concurrency control | duplicate/concurrent Begin cannot cause a second spawn | memory-only; no durable host ledger |
| Job Object + suspended launch | Windows process containment | target cannot run before required tree containment is established | assignment failure is fail-closed |
| native handle ownership + inherited-handle allowlist | Windows object identity / least privilege | no PID-only kill authority and no accidental capability-handle leak | PID remains receipt data |
| Core-owned UNKNOWN/reconciliation | side-effect consistency / controller reconciliation | no blind retry after lost acknowledgement | WorkingState remains the sole durable owner |
| exact compiler/binary provenance | software supply chain | qualification binds exact executed host bytes/toolchain | no floating toolchain acceptance |

ConPTY and sandboxing are researched as adjacent future mechanisms but are outside the first implementation slice; adding them later is a stage sub-entry because they introduce terminal-input and security primitives.

### 1. One short-lived host per operation

First slice is **not a daemon**. One host process owns at most one active native operation. This removes daemon discovery, ACL/auth, reconnect, multiplexing and durable host-session state.

### 2. Private framed stdio

Selected transport is parent-created anonymous stdin/stdout pipes with a bounded length frame (`u32` length + UTF-8 JSON), explicit `protocol_version`, strict message enums and per-field limits. Stdout is protocol-only; diagnostics are stderr.

No TCP/HTTP listener, named-pipe service, port discovery or public RPC endpoint is introduced.

Initial correlation fields are `host_instance_id`, `request_id`, `logical_operation_id`, `attempt_id`, `authorization_ref`. The host treats authorization_ref only as correlation evidence; it cannot refresh or widen it.

The execution payload is typed `executable + argv + cwd + bounded_env`, never a Chat-facing `run_anything(command)` or raw shell string.

### 3. No host-side durable dedup ledger

The narrower lifecycle closes the #132 open question without SQLite/WAL/queue state:

- host accepts only one active Begin;
- duplicate/concurrent Begin in the same host is rejected before a second spawn;
- once delivery may have begun, missing terminal acknowledgement is ambiguous;
- a restarted host never auto-replays the unresolved attempt;
- CAP WorkingState remains the sole durable owner of `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` and reconciliation;
- another physical attempt requires fresh `CONFIRMED_NOT_APPLIED` plus normal grant/LoopGuard/budget checks.

Required observable invariant remains: **at most one physical spawn for an authorized attempt before reconciliation**.

### 4. Windows containment ordering

Selected first-slice process path:

```text
create/configure Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE
 -> create target suspended
 -> assign target to Job
 -> assignment succeeds
 -> resume target
```

No breakaway flag and **no compatibility fallback that resumes an uncontained consequence-bearing process**. Job/native process handles are the ownership identity; PID is receipt data only.

Handle inheritance must be explicit/allowlisted so protocol pipes, Job handles and unrelated resources do not leak into the child tree.

Parent protocol EOF is owner loss: terminate the active Job/tree, close/reap handles and exit.

### 5. Cancellation / completion

Safety cancellation is whole-Job termination, not generic Ctrl+C. Windows console control events are process-group/console constrained; graceful interrupt may later exist as best-effort behavior but cannot be the cleanup invariant.

Root-process exit is not tree completion. The host retains the Job and observes Job active-process state so descendants cannot be silently left running.

### 6. Bounded non-lossy output

Child stdout/stderr are bytes, not trusted text and not permission. The host must chunk/encode them into bounded protocol events without a lossy internal broadcast queue. Backpressure is allowed; silent dropping is not.

Each operation carries an authorized output budget. If the budget is exceeded or the protocol consumer cannot be maintained, terminate/fail the operation explicitly and report truncation/overflow rather than returning a normal-looking success with missing evidence.

### 7. Toolchain / binary provenance

Production implementation must pin an exact reviewed compiler and Cargo.lock. At research time Rust 1.98.1 is current; it is itself a patch fixing a 1.98.0 rustc vtable miscompilation, so a floating `stable` channel is insufficient release evidence.

Current `windows-sys` is the preferred thin Win32 binding candidate behind one audited platform module; actual versions are re-resolved at implementation time after Core freeze.

## Problem evidence

1. Native process ownership is distinct from PID/process-object convenience APIs.
2. Containment ordering matters: assignment after a process is already running leaves a pre-assignment window.
3. Broad inherited handles can leak files/sockets/tokens; Windows supports exact inherited-handle lists.
4. Root exit does not prove descendant-tree exit.
5. Transport ACK is not effect success; CAP already has UNKNOWN/reconciliation semantics that must remain authoritative.
6. Python/Node/PowerShell are not being replaced because they are 'bad'; the new role is only the low-level lifecycle seam after Core freeze.

## Solution evidence — engineering domain

Primary Windows sources researched:

- Job Objects — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/procthread/job-objects
- AssignProcessToJobObject — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/jobapi2/nf-jobapi2-assignprocesstojobobject
- Creating processes / handle inheritance — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/procthread/creating-processes
- Handle inheritance — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/procthread/inheritance
- CreatePseudoConsole — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/console/createpseudoconsole
- GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/console/generateconsolectrlevent
- Job accounting / ActiveProcesses — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winnt/ns-winnt-jobobject_basic_accounting_information

Relevant guarantees: Job Objects manage process groups as a unit; `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` kills associated processes on final Job-handle close; children normally inherit Job membership; nested Job assignment can fail and must be handled; STARTUPINFOEX handle lists bound inheritance; ActiveProcesses gives native tree accounting.

## Source-code evidence

Research date: **2026-09-23**.

### OpenAI Codex

`openai/codex@27969c0ae9c1ec23e359ff5133b4c36a8dd5b1ac`

Inspected:
- `codex-rs/core/src/spawn.rs`
- `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/win/job.rs`
- `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/win/conpty.rs`
- `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/win/psuedocon_tests.rs`

Classification: **OPEN_IMPLEMENTED** for inspected spawn/Job/ConPTY paths.

Current code provides KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE Job ownership, suspended-spawn + assign-before-resume, native process-handle termination, and current ConPTY tests for output closure/descendant/termination behavior. A separate compatibility helper may resume after assignment failure; CAP explicitly does **not** copy that fallback for its consequence-bearing path.

Lesson: **ADAPT_MECHANIC / REFERENCE_ONLY**. Do not import Codex planning/session authority.

### Goose

`aaif-goose/goose@201837dffc92ac3cce7ce7c3b3bb8fe4153dcc4b`

Inspected:
- `crates/goose/src/subprocess.rs`
- `crates/goose/tests/subprocess_cleanup.rs`

Classification: **OPEN_IMPLEMENTED** for inspected Linux owner-death mechanics.

Goose uses process groups plus `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` with parent identity recheck. Direct tests prove child death after true parent-process death and prove a long-lived child does not accidentally bind its lifetime to a temporary spawning thread.

Lesson: **ADAPT_MECHANIC / REFERENCE_ONLY**. CAP must test real owner death, not merely call `Child::kill()`.

## Failure lessons from current implementations / reports

- **Orphaned Windows descendants are a real operational failure class.** Recent Codex issue reports (#21994, #34614, #35726) describe parent/session termination paths that left grandchildren alive where Job containment was absent or not applied to that spawn path. These are issue reports, not independent proof of every root-cause claim, but they reinforce testing the exact owner-death path rather than assuming one shared helper protects all spawns.
- **Job containment and daemon detachment conflict by design.** Codex issue #44503 reports daemon startup being blocked by host Job semantics on one Windows environment. Native Host v1 therefore stays short-lived/owned and does not combine 'must die with owner' with daemon-detachment behavior.
- **PTY teardown is timing-sensitive.** Current Codex Windows PTY tests explicitly exercise descendant survival and termination; issue reports such as #14679/#25272 show teardown/AttachConsole failures in adjacent node-pty paths. CAP separates PTY from the first process slice rather than treating it as a trivial wrapper.
- **Lossy asynchronous output queues can corrupt evidence.** Codex issue #45540 reports multi-megabyte Windows output losing bytes when a broadcast consumer lagged. Native Host uses bounded backpressure and explicit output-limit failure; it must never silently discard output and still report normal completion.
- **Compiler provenance is consequence-relevant.** Rust 1.98.1 fixes a 1.98.0 rustc vtable miscompilation. Release evidence therefore pins an exact reviewed patch toolchain rather than mutable `stable`.

These lessons are used as failure hypotheses and test requirements; they do not make external projects part of CAP's trust boundary.

## Fit to this architecture

The selected design consumes the Core-v1 seam instead of creating another framework: Core owns why/when an effect is allowed and how ambiguity is reconciled; Native Host owns only the OS lifecycle needed to execute one already-authorized effect. Provider/native receipt remains evidence, and fresh project observation still determines verification.

The first slice intentionally excludes interactive PTY and sandbox policy because both add authority/security semantics beyond process ownership. That is narrowing the implementation goal, not weakening the final product boundary.

## Alternatives

### A — keep native lifecycle scattered in Python/Node/PowerShell

No new toolchain, but Job/native handle/strict inheritance/later ConPTY ownership remains split across higher-level runtimes and capability glue. **Not selected for the Native Host role**; those runtimes remain valid above the boundary.

### B — long-lived Rust daemon over named pipe/HTTP

Adds endpoint ACL/auth, daemon upgrade/version skew, reconnect, multi-client concurrency and pressure for durable host state/generic dispatch. **REJECT for v1**.

### C — one-operation Rust child over framed stdio

No discoverable endpoint, no durable host state, one attempt per lifetime, small provenance surface, natural Job/native-handle ownership. **SELECT / NARROW**.

### D — revive historical Rust-first CAP

Would replace/duplicate accepted Core, WorkingState, semantic projection and policy roles. **REJECT**.

## Minimum sufficient first implementation slice

After Core freeze only:

```text
one exact-version Rust binary
one versioned bounded stdio protocol
one active operation per host
Windows non-interactive process execution only
Job Object containment
suspended -> assign -> resume
native handle ownership
bounded stdout/stderr evidence
whole-tree hard cancel
owner-EOF cleanup
no PTY input
no sandbox
no daemon
no host durable state
no new Chat tool
```

ConPTY interactive input/resize, graceful interrupt policy, restricted-token/AppContainer sandboxing, persistent host sessions, cross-platform parity, generic Local Execution and host-side durable queues are **outside this first-slice goal** and require their own later slice/re-entry where they introduce new authority/security primitives.

## Failure / crash matrix

| Failure boundary | Required behavior | Extra spawn before reconciliation |
|---|---|---:|
| binary/hash/protocol mismatch | unavailable/reject before target | 0 |
| malformed/partial/oversized frame | fail closed; no target | 0 |
| duplicate Begin | reject before second create | 0 |
| Job creation/config failure | fail closed | 0 |
| target created suspended; Job assignment fails | terminate/reap before resume | 0 runnable targets |
| assigned; host crash before resume | Job close cleans contained target; missing receipt remains conservative | 0 additional |
| resumed; Spawned ACK lost | Core `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`; no replay | 0 additional |
| host crash with active tree | Job close kills tree; Core reconciles external effects | 0 additional |
| parent/adapter dies | stdio EOF -> host kills Job/tree and exits | 0 additional |
| root exits while descendant remains | do not call tree complete; observe Job active-process state | 0 |
| cancel races exit | one terminal host state | 0 |
| nested-Job assignment incompatibility | fail closed; no uncontained resume | 0 runnable targets |
| PID reused | retained native handle governs ownership | 0 |
| protocol/Job handle inherited by target | qualification failure; implementation must structurally prevent | 0 |
| host restart after unresolved attempt | never replay old attempt automatically | 0 |
| Core says CONFIRMED_APPLIED / STILL_UNKNOWN | no respawn | 0 |
| Core says CONFIRMED_NOT_APPLIED | new attempt still needs fresh normal authorization | one separately authorized attempt |
| compiler/binary provenance moves | acceptance/review stale | 0 |
| machine/power loss | outside first-slice process-lifetime guarantee; Core fails closed/reconciles | 0 |

No release-critical cell in the selected first-slice process-lifetime scope permits blind re-spawn.

## Failure shields / acceptance ladder

### L1 protocol/state machine
- strict version + enum + size bounds;
- exactly one Begin;
- duplicate cannot spawn;
- stdout protocol-only;
- no raw shell command surface;
- host receipt cannot directly map to project PASS/DONE.

### L2 Windows lifecycle
- prove Job exists/configured before runnable child;
- assignment failure leaves no runnable target;
- child + grandchild die on cancel;
- hard parent death -> EOF -> host + descendants gone;
- exact handle inheritance allowlist;
- root-exit + surviving descendant is not falsely terminal;
- cancel/completion race has one terminal host state;
- identity-sensitive operations retain process handles.

### L2 CAP ambiguity integration
- inject crash after resume/before receipt;
- record unresolved/UNKNOWN;
- restart performs zero replay;
- CONFIRMED_APPLIED and STILL_UNKNOWN never respawn;
- CONFIRMED_NOT_APPLIED still requires a newly authorized attempt.

### Supply-chain / provenance
- exact Rust toolchain;
- committed Cargo.lock;
- dependency license/security checks;
- exact built/installed host hash in runtime receipt;
- source/runtime provenance in release-critical evidence.

### Review / physical
Production implementation requires hosted Windows CI/security, mandatory fresh ordinary-Chat exact BASE..HEAD semantic review, then target-Windows process-tree/owner-loss physical qualification on the reviewed head. Ordinary-Chat L3 is required only when a concrete Chat-facing capability consumes this host.

## Complexity budget

Adds only: one Rust binary, one private protocol/state machine, one Windows lifecycle module and one capability-adapter binding.

Explicitly avoids: RPC framework, service manager, listener, database/WAL, provider registry, scheduler/event bus, new public tool, second authorization system, second verifier, second WorkingState.

## Falsifiers / mandatory re-entry

Re-enter Stage Research if one-operation stdio cannot provide owner-loss semantics; a durable host-side replay/dedup store becomes necessary; first consumer requires interactive PTY or AppContainer/restricted-token sandboxing; nested-Job behavior prevents fail-closed contained spawn on supported Windows; or implementation creates a generic command runner reachable through existing public tools.

## Repository changes

- durable boundary recorded in `project-context/ARCHITECTURE.md`;
- new native-systems role recorded in `project-context/ARCHITECTURE_REUSE_BASELINE.md`;
- **zero production runtime changes**.
